newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli stocks lower ahead of decision in corruption scandal.
newsitem.headline: Israeli stocks lower ahead of decision in corruption scandal.

text.p: Israeli stocks closed slightly lower Sunday as investors waited to see if the attorney-general would charge Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a corruption scandal.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 stocks fell 0.64 percent, or 1.59 points, to 247.68 on a turnover of 95 million shekels against 99 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
An official announcement by the attorney-general on whether Netanyahu was announced after the end of the trading day.

Last week police recommended the prime minister and three officials be charged with fraud and breach of trust over the short-lived appointment of political crony Roni Bar-On as attorney-general in January.
On Monday and Tuesday the stock exchange will remain closed for the Jewish holiday of Passover.

"The market is on hold today as investors wait for the attorney-general's decision. Despite that, the market continues to show strength and it remained mixed and balanced today," said Zvi Hoffman at Meitav Investments and Securities.
"Political uncertainty is not good for the market and if we are going to face a political turmoil the market will remain very nervous," Hoffman said.
